title: Anatomy Paper 7: Neuroanatomy, Development and Body Organisation
source: Adapted from user-provided Dentistry past paper questions (Anatomy pages)

objective.question: The nervous cells are called:
objective.explanation: Neurons (nerve cells) are the structural and functional units of nervous tissue; axons and myelin sheaths are parts of a neuron and nerves are bundles of fibres.

objective.question: Any muscle of the human body has:
objective.explanation: Skeletal muscles are described by their origin (more fixed attachment) and insertion (more movable attachment).

objective.question: Foot inversion is the movement in which the sole turns:
objective.explanation: Inversion turns the plantar surface medially. It is one component of supination, which also includes adduction and plantar flexion.

objective.question: The small intestine is divided into:
objective.explanation: The small intestine consists of the duodenum, jejunum and ileum; pylorus and fundus are parts of the stomach.

objective.question: Coronal and sagittal planes are examples of:
objective.explanation: The coronal, sagittal, transverse (horizontal) and median planes are the standard anatomical planes used to describe sections of the body.

objective.question: The tissue types include:
options: Epithelial, connective, muscle and nervous tissue
objective.explanation: The body has four basic tissue types: epithelial, connective (including bone, cartilage and blood), muscle and nervous tissue.

objective.question: Which nerve innervates the quadriceps femoris muscle group?
objective.explanation: The femoral nerve supplies the quadriceps femoris in the anterior compartment of the thigh.

objective.question: Which bone forms the lateral malleolus at the ankle?
objective.explanation: The distal fibula forms the lateral malleolus; the distal tibia forms the medial malleolus.

objective.question: The largest nerve in the human body is the:
objective.explanation: The sciatic nerve (L4-S3), formed in the greater sciatic foramen, is the largest and thickest nerve of the body.

objective.question: The head of the humerus articulates with the:
objective.explanation: The rounded head of the humerus fits into the shallow glenoid cavity of the scapula to form the shoulder joint.

objective.question: During the second week of development, the embryonic disc consists of:
objective.explanation: In the second week the bilaminar embryonic disc is formed of epiblast and hypoblast; the germ layers (ectoderm, mesoderm, endoderm) appear in the third week.

objective.question: HCG stands for:
objective.explanation: Human chorionic gonadotropin is secreted by the trophoblast/placenta and is the hormone detected in pregnancy tests.

objective.question: The median plane divides the body into:
objective.explanation: The median (midsagittal) plane runs longitudinally through the midline, dividing the body into equal right and left parts.

objective.question: Cranial nerves are so called because they:
options: Are part of the central nervous system
objective.explanation: The twelve cranial nerves emerge directly from the brain (brainstem), in contrast to the spinal nerves that arise from the spinal cord.

objective.question: White blood cells are divided into:
objective.explanation: Leucocytes are classified as granulocytes (neutrophils, eosinophils, basophils) and agranulocytes (lymphocytes, monocytes).

objective.question: The tenth cranial nerve is the:
objective.explanation: The vagus nerve (CN X) is the tenth cranial nerve and supplies the pharynx, larynx and thoracic and abdominal viscera.

objective.question: The central nervous system is divided into:
objective.explanation: The central nervous system comprises the brain and the spinal cord; the peripheral nervous system contains the cranial and spinal nerves.

objective.question: The two divisions of the pelvic cavity are the:
objective.explanation: The greater (false) pelvis lies above the pelvic brim and is continuous with the abdomen; the lesser (true) pelvis lies below the brim.

objective.question: Which bone contains the sella turcica that houses the pituitary gland?
objective.explanation: The sella turcica is a depression in the sphenoid bone that contains the pituitary gland.

objective.question: Which lymphatic duct drains the right side of the head and neck?
objective.explanation: The right lymphatic duct receives lymph from the right upper quadrant, including the right side of the head and neck.

structured.question: Name the four rotator cuff muscles. (4 marks)
markingGuide: Supraspinatus
Infraspinatus
Teres minor
Subscapularis
structured.modelAnswer: The rotator cuff muscles are the supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and subscapularis (mnemonic SITS); they stabilise the shoulder joint by holding the head of the humerus in the glenoid cavity.

structured.question: Draw and label the structure of the stomach. (4 marks)
markingGuide: Drawing showing cardia, fundus, body, pyloric antrum and pylorus
Labels for lesser and greater curvatures
Labels for cardiac, pyloric and sphincters/oesophageal opening
One mark for a labelled drawing, one per correct set of labels
structured.modelAnswer: The stomach is a J-shaped organ with a cardia (where the oesophagus enters), a dome-shaped fundus, a body, and a pyloric part (antrum and canal) ending at the pylorus; it has a lesser and a greater curvature and its openings (cardiac and pyloric) are guarded by sphincters.

structured.question: Give the names of the major abdominal organs. (4 marks)
markingGuide: Stomach, liver, gall bladder, pancreas
Small intestine (duodenum, jejunum, ileum)
Large intestine (caecum, colon, rectum)
Spleen and kidneys/ureters (credit any four correct organs)
structured.modelAnswer: The major abdominal organs are the stomach, liver, gall bladder, pancreas, spleen, the small intestine (duodenum, jejunum and ileum) and the large intestine (caecum, colon and rectum), together with the kidneys and ureters.

structured.question: Draw and label the structure of a neurone. (4 marks)
markingGuide: Drawing showing cell body (soma) with nucleus and dendrites
Label for the axon with its myelin sheath and nodes of Ranvier
Label for terminal branches/end bulbs (synaptic knobs)
Labels for axon hillock and Schwann cell as appropriate
structured.modelAnswer: A neurone consists of a cell body (soma) containing the nucleus with branching dendrites receiving impulses; a single long axon, often insulated by a myelin sheath with nodes of Ranvier; and terminal branches ending in synaptic knobs that release neurotransmitter at the synapse.

structured.question: Name the tarsal bones and the wrist bones (carpal bones). (4 marks)
markingGuide: Tarsals: calcaneus, talus, navicular, cuboid and the three cuneiforms
Carpals: scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate and hamate
Two marks for each complete or near-complete list
Accept spelling variants
structured.modelAnswer: The seven tarsal bones are the calcaneus, talus, navicular, cuboid and medial, intermediate and lateral cuneiforms. The eight carpal bones of the wrist are the scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform, trapezium, trapezoid, capitate and hamate, arranged in proximal and distal rows.
